title: Yen's slide to weekly loss prompts bets for another intervention

content_html:
Reuters

Thu, August 13, 2026 at 6:47 PM MST 3 min read

SINGAPORE, Aug 14 (Reuters) - The yen headed for its biggest weekly loss in three months on Friday as the impact of U.S. and Japanese intervention faded, leaving traders to wager another round of official buying would be needed to stem ‌the rot.

The currency has surrendered roughly half the gains sparked by intervention in late July and early August, falling about 1% ‌this week to 159.43 per dollar. It was trading near 164 per dollar before July's intervention and traders see the 160 level as a potential trigger for fresh official action.

The ​yen's retreat is set to be its biggest weekly drop since May, when it was also backsliding after a round of official buying. A fall of about 0.8% to 183.91 yen per euro this week is the largest since April.

The Japanese currency was stable early on Friday but has been falling for years, and was at near four-decade lows before the intervention, on a combination of perennially low interest rates and newer confidence concerns around government ‌spending and funding.

The broader currency market has been ⁠fairly steady this week, with support for the dollar from higher oil prices and Middle East tension offset by benign U.S. jobs and inflation reports that reduced expectations for U.S. interest rate hikes.

Overnight figures showing unchanged U.S. producer ⁠prices in July further supported dialling back bets on a September hike, now seen as a roughly 35% chance.

The euro edged 0.2% lower to $1.1536 this week while sterling was flat at $1.3489. A surprisingly low inflation expectations reading knocked the New Zealand dollar on Thursday, but it bounced back as the swap market stuck ​with ​an 85% chance of a rate hike in September.

The Australian dollar hovered at $0.7060. [AUD/]

THE ​ONUS IS ON BOJ

Japan may conduct more joint yen intervention "at ‌any time" and signal the chance of faster-than-expected interest rate hikes to stem further falls, Tokyo's former top currency diplomat Mitsuhiro Furusawa told Reuters in an interview.

Markets have already bet on the Bank of Japan raising rates further and sooner than previously expected after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Japan should reinforce currency intervention with policies and fundamentals that underpin the yen.

"It's not much of a surprise that the yen has retraced," said OCBC strategist Sim Moh Siong.

"Because for the intervention to change the yen trend, we need to see a more hawkish BOJ stance, which ‌the market is trying to price in, but at the same time, we ​need validation," he said. "The onus is on BOJ to step up."

content_html_zh:
路透社

2026 年 8 月 13 日星期四下午 6:47（MST） 阅读时间 3 分钟

路透新加坡 8 月 14 日 - 随着美国和日本干预措施的影响消退，日元周五录得三个月来最大单周跌幅，交易员押注需要进行另一轮官方买盘才能阻止日元贬值。

该货币已经回吐了 7 月底和 8 月初干预措施带来的涨幅的大约一半，本周下跌约 1%，至 159.43 美元兑 159.43 美元。 在 7 月份干预之前，美元兑美元汇率接近 164 美元，交易员认为 160 美元兑美元汇率可能会触发新的官方行动。

日元的回落将是自 5 月份以来的最大单周跌幅，当时日元在一轮官方买盘后也出现了回落。 本周日元兑欧元下跌约 0.8% 至 183.91，为 4 月份以来最大跌幅。

日元周五早些时候保持稳定，但多年来一直在下跌，并且在干预前处于近四个十年的低点，原因是长期的低利率和对政府支出和融资的新的信心担忧。

本周，更广泛的货币市场相当稳定，油价上涨和中东紧张局势对美元的支撑被美国良好的就业和通胀报告所抵消，这些报告降低了对美国加息的预期。

隔夜数据显示 7 月份美国生产者价格保持不变，进一步支持了对 9 月份加息的押注，目前认为加息的可能性约为 35%。

欧元本周小幅下跌 0.2% 至 1.1536 美元，而英镑则持平于 1.3489 美元。 令人惊讶的低通胀预期数据周四对新西兰元造成打击，但随着掉期市场坚持 9 月加息的可能性为 85%，新西兰元反弹。

澳元兑美元徘徊在0.7060美元。 [澳元/]

日本央行有责任

东京前首席货币外交官 Mitsuhiro Furusawa 在接受路透社采访时表示，日本可能“随时”进行更多联合日元干预，并暗示可能会以快于预期的速度加息，以阻止日元进一步下跌。

在美国财长斯科特·贝森特表示日本应通过支撑日元的政策和基本面加强货币干预后，市场已经押注日本央行将比此前预期进一步加息。

华侨银行策略师 Sim Moh Siong 表示：“日元回落并不令人意外。”

他表示：“因为要通过干预来改变日元趋势，我们需要看到日本央行采取更加强硬的立场，市场正在试图消化这一立场，但与此同时，我们需要得到验证。” “日本央行有责任采取行动。”
